stem: Which self-care plan should the nurse recommend to an adult experiencing ongoing work-related stress?

options.A: Include regular physical activity, adequate sleep, relaxation practices, and connection with supportive people.
options.B: Wait for the stressor to disappear without using deliberate coping or recovery strategies.
options.C: Avoid physical activity during stressful periods to conserve energy for work.
options.D: Use caffeine and alcohol as primary strategies to manage stress and sleep.

rationale: Current CDC stress-management guidance recommends caring for the body with adequate sleep and physical activity, taking time to unwind with practices such as deep breathing or meditation, and connecting with trusted people or community supports. A is correct.
educational_objective: Identify evidence-based health behaviors that support stress management and well-being.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_locator: Take care of your body; Make time to unwind; Connect with others
source_claim_supported: Stress management includes adequate sleep, physical activity, relaxation/unwinding practices, and supportive social connection.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — healthy lifestyle, coping, and wellness education
blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — stress management

source_original.stem: A nurse is providing health promotion counseling to a client experiencing significant work-related stress. Evidence-based stress management strategies the nurse might suggest include:

options.A: Use regular activity, relaxation skills, adequate sleep, and supportive social connections
options.B: Wait for workplace stress to resolve without using any deliberate coping or recovery strategy
options.C: Reduce physical activity during stressful periods to conserve energy for work responsibilities
options.D: Rely on caffeine and alcohol to manage stress, improve sleep, and maintain daily performance

source_original.rationale: Evidence-based stress management strategies include regular physical activity, relaxation techniques (such as deep breathing, mindfulness, or meditation), adequate sleep, maintaining social connections/support, and, when needed, professional support — all of which can help mitigate the negative health effects of chronic stress.
source_original.source_detail: CDC/NIOSH stress resources: physical activity, relaxation, sleep, and social support; reviewed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Updated to CDC's current 2026 Managing Stress page and limited the keyed answer to recommendations explicitly present there; retained Health Promotion and Maintenance mapping.

audit_findings.claim_audit: Sleep, activity, relaxation/unwinding and supportive connection are directly supported.

distractor_audit.D: Not a recommended stress-management strategy and may worsen health/sleep.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: A uniquely contains the CDC-supported behaviors.
audit_findings.cueing: Parallel self-care plans; no narrative cue.
audit_findings.blueprint: Wellness and coping education fit Health Promotion and Maintenance.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked CDC current page; A remains unique.
